title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction: This page is part of the notational set-up for the 1976 IHES talk on the divided-power de Rham complex. It continues the previous page's statement of the Dold–Kan (here 'Dold–Puppe') correspondence. For an additive Karoubian (idempotent-complete) category A there is an equivalence between simplicial objects A_* and nonnegatively graded chain complexes A_•. One direction is ND ('non-degenerate', i.e. the normalized chain complex); the other is DP (Dold–Puppe, i.e. Γ). Grothendieck fixes a convention: one letter K denotes both avatars. K_* = (n ↦ K_[n]) is the simplicial object, with bracketed components. K_• = (K_n, d_n)_{n≥0} is the chain complex, and K_• = ND_•(K_*), K_* = DP_*(K_•). He remarks, with an exclamation mark, that this forces the unusual notation K_[n] for simplicial components, since K_n is reserved for the chain components. Dually, applying the theory to A^op gives the cosimplicial Dold–Kan equivalence A^* ≃ A^· (cosimplicial objects versus nonnegative cochain complexes). The notation there is K^· = ND^·(K^*), K^* = DP^*(K^·), K^* = (n ↦ K^[n]), K^· = (K^n, d^n). He notes that ND and DP commute with additive functors. This holds because additive functors preserve finite direct sums and split idempotents, which are all the constructions need. In particular, for a duality equivalence A ≃ B^op (introduced earlier), the four avatars correspond under the raising and lowering of indices. A single letter K can then denote four objects K^*, K_*, K^·, K_•, as the next page spells out. The purpose is bookkeeping for the later study of cosimplicial algebras and the divided-power de Rham complex as homotopy invariants. The goal is to localize categories of algebraic structures (complexes, cosimplicial algebras) at maps coming from homotopy equivalences.
errors: No mathematical errors. The claim that ND and DP commute with additive functors is correct for additive functors between Karoubian additive categories, since the normalized complex can be written as a direct summand cut out by idempotents.

ideas.what: Dold–Kan equivalence between simplicial objects and nonnegative chain complexes in an idempotent-complete additive category
ideas.usually_credited_to: Dold (1958), Kan (1958), Dold–Puppe (1961); general Karoubian form folklore, e.g. Lurie HA 1.2.3
ideas.where_published: Used implicitly in Illusie's Complexe cotangent (1971–72) in Grothendieck's circle; not stated by Grothendieck himself to my knowledge

ideas.what: Cosimplicial Dold–Kan equivalence between cosimplicial objects and cochain complexes, obtained by passing to A^op
Compatibility of the N and Γ functors with additive functors, and with dualities A ≃ B^op exchanging simplicial/chain and cosimplicial/cochain avatars
ideas.modern_name: Naturality of Dold–Kan under additive functors

ideas.what: Notational convention K_[n] versus K_n (and K^[n] versus K^n) distinguishing simplicial components from chain components

deep.surprise_reason: Purely notational and expository page restating the standard (co)simplicial Dold–Kan correspondence and its functoriality; nothing beyond folklore.
transcription_corrections: 'De même, la théorie des DP s'applique' — the image reads roughly 'De =, la théorie des DP s'applique : A' (the trailing 'A' probably begins the next line). The '(≈)' belongs on the arrows of the displayed equivalence, not after it.
'la conversion de la montée en la descente des indices' is more plausibly 'la convention de la montée ou de la descente des indices'.
Last line: 'Donc dans ce cas, la [même] lettre K désignera' — the image shows '= lettre K', echoing the earlier '= lettre' shorthand for 'même lettre'.
